summary.notes:
## **Survey Data Processing and Participant Management**

The team confirmed key data cleanup and participant updates would be completed promptly to ensure accurate final reporting.

- **Completion of survey refresh and participant removal planned within hours** (01:33)  
    - The survey driver updates and removal of **63 participants** from SCCL will be executed after the call.  
    - Karthik Rao committed to running the refresh script post-call and confirming completion within **1-2 hours**.  
    - This update is essential to finalize the survey results for the communication report.  
    - Anne Baehnman will receive an email confirmation once this process is complete.

- **Clarification on participant counts and unanswered responses** (01:56)  
    - Karthik identified a discrepancy between **137 total participants** and **127 visible in exports**, with **98 unanswered responses** matching exactly.  
    - He has shared the full export with Danielle for verification and will follow up if further checking is needed.  
    - The match of **63 removed participants** aligns with the unanswered count, ensuring data integrity.

- **Consideration of employee status in participation data** (02:47)  
    - Discussion confirmed the data upload in February included only **active employees at that time**, not those on long-term leave.  
    - Some people on leave or no longer with the company might still appear due to timing of data extraction.  
    - This approach reflects a snapshot in time consistent with survey methodology.

- **Activation of sub-admin access to reporting platform planned** (41:01)  
    - Sub-admin roles for team leaders will likely be enabled after data cleanup and reporting setup are finalized.  
    - Karthik will demonstrate current platform capabilities first before enabling this feature, expected **tomorrow**.

## **Thematic Analysis and Reporting Strategy**

The team aligned on an approach to analyze free-text survey responses for communication strengths and challenges, balancing detail and data quality.

- **Use of all four open-text questions for thematic analysis recommended** (08:04)  
    - Anne Baehnman emphasized pulling themes from responses across **all four open-ended questions** to capture both strengths and challenges fully.  
    - Nirupa agreed, noting a day's time is needed to review responses for feasibility and theme extraction.  
    - Karthik suggested mapping responses to strengths or weaknesses after review to confirm what can be reported.  
    - Thematic analysis results and format will be shared by **tomorrow morning**.

- **Graphical presentations based on rating questions planned** (16:14)  
    - Visual summaries such as **pie charts and graphs** will represent data from key grid/rating questions.  
    - These will include filters by **business unit, business group, team, and region** as requested.  
    - Karthik clarified that sufficient response volume is needed for meaningful segmentation, but full filtering will be supported.

- **Filtering thematic analysis by organizational attributes confirmed necessary** (15:21)  
    - Despite potential sparse comments in smaller groups, Anne and Kasey insisted on breakdowns by **team, sub-team, business group, and region** for actionable insights.  
    - Karthik acknowledged this requirement, and Nirupa agreed to proceed with full attribute filtering.

- **Top five strengths and challenges labeling may be adjusted based on data** (16:47)  
    - If the data does not support clear top five strengths/challenges, the team will propose alternative thematic summaries.  
    - This flexibility ensures the final report reflects meaningful patterns rather than forced categories.

## **Action Plan and Scoring Criteria**

The team outlined criteria and reporting filters for the action plan based on driver scores, ensuring targeted follow-up.

- **Action plans triggered by driver scores below 7.4 across all drivers** (17:12)  
    - Managers will receive action plans if their driver scores fall **below 7.4**, but not all managers are included, only those with low scores.  
    - The same four filters (business unit, group, team, region) will be applied to these action plans for granularity.

- **Filter-based reporting for action plans confirmed feasible** (18:21)  
    - Nirupa confirmed that incorporating filters with driver scores for action plan generation is straightforward.  
    - Full report structure and timeline for this will be shared alongside thematic analysis by **tomorrow**.

## **Regression and Correlation Analysis Decision**

The team decided to omit regression analysis due to the survey’s communication focus and lack of meaningful engagement driver variation.

- **Regression analysis deemed not meaningful for this communication survey** (19:15)  
    - Atish explained regression is typically useful in engagement surveys to identify key drivers of overall engagement.  
    - Since all drivers measured relate to communication, correlation/regression would not reveal actionable insights.  
    - The team agreed to exclude this analysis from the final reports.

- **Optional questions in regression analysis cause data disruption** (23:14)  
    - Atish showed some survey items related to tool usage are optional and would skew regression results.  
    - This further supports the decision to omit regression for clarity and data quality.

- **Team will provide visibility of regression questions for reference** (20:36)  
    - Atish offered to share the specific questions considered for regression to inform Anne’s understanding, though analysis will not be pursued.

## **Reporting Timeline and Deliverables**

Clear delivery dates and report batch plans were established to meet stakeholder deadlines.

- **Final reports planned in two batches on April 13 and April 17** (22:27)  
    - Karthik confirmed the goal to deliver all survey reports in **two batches** before Anne’s deadline of **April 21**.  
    - The first batch includes thematic and action plan reports; the second covers remaining items such as tenure data.

- **Report format and structure to be shared by tomorrow** (25:45)  
    - The team will provide a detailed outline of each report’s contents and format.  
    - This includes clarifications on thematic presentation, graphical elements, and filter usage.

- **Survey data refresh and participant removal to be completed before report generation** (26:06)  
    - The refreshed and cleaned data set will enable accurate reporting starting tomorrow morning.

## **Platform Usability and Data Visualization**

Discussions addressed platform filtering, visualization limitations, and improvements needed for sub-admin users.

- **Current platform shows counts but not percentages when filtered by team** (26:45)  
    - Anne noted filtering by team changes display from global percentages to response counts without clear percentages.  
    - This reduces usability for sub-admins wanting to see proportional data for their teams.

- **Karthik committed to enabling percentage and pie chart views for multi-select questions** (29:11)  
    - A feature exists for rating questions but not yet enabled for multi-select and single-select questions.  
    - He will check with engineering to enable these views for sub-admins for better data insight by tomorrow.

- **Manual work currently required to create percentage-based charts for filtered data** (34:29)  
    - Anne highlighted the difficulty sub-admins face in manually calculating percentages from raw counts to share with teams.  
    - Karthik acknowledged this inefficiency and aims to improve automated visualization.

- **Insight page offers detailed positive/neutral/negative breakdowns for engagement drivers** (35:54)  
    - Karthik demonstrated a page that breaks down rating responses by sentiment and filters for super admins.  
    - This feature might be extended to cover single- and multi-select questions for all admin roles pending technical confirmation.

- **Sub-admin experience critical for executive leaders requiring detailed team data** (34:29)  
    - Anne emphasized different leadership levels expect varying data granularity.  
    - Enhancing sub-admin reports to match these expectations is a priority to support decision making.

## **Next Steps and Meeting Coordination**

The team arranged follow-up meetings and communication to continue progress and address outstanding questions.

- **Follow-up call scheduled for tomorrow at 8:00 AM PST for engagement and communication survey review** (39:38)  
    - Karthik will send calendar invite post current meeting to include Amanda Meer Herring and other stakeholders.  
    - This call will allow reviewing platform walkthrough and outstanding questions.

- **Karthik will email Anne today with confirmation on driver updates and participant removals** (40:44)  
    - This ensures Anne is informed when data refresh completes and final datasets are ready.

- **Additional questions Anne has will be addressed in tomorrow’s call or via email as needed** (37:45)  
    - Karthik offered to extend the discussion and provide detailed platform walkthroughs in follow-up.  
    - This flexible approach aims to minimize disruption while ensuring full clarity.

- **Team to provide full report timelines and format details by tomorrow** (25:36)  
    - Nirupa confirmed that timelines and report structure information will be finalized internally and shared promptly.

summary.notes:
## **Engagement Survey Reporting**

The meeting clarified the structure and content of the engagement survey reports to help the HR team better understand and act on the data.

- **Overview of report types and key metrics** explained by Sivanandh, including two main reports: an AI-based PDF report with detailed question breakdowns and an executive summary showing overall engagement scores and participation rates (09:01)
    - The executive summary highlights total participants (**925**), completion rates, and highest response day with **210 responses on 27th February**
    - Identified that **43 employees started but did not complete the survey**, with **24 from one team**, signaling a target for improved participation
    - Sivanandh stressed the importance of investigating non-participation reasons to increase future survey completion to **95-96%**

- **Detailed AI-powered PDF report insights** covering engagement scores, ENPS scores, and driver analysis (14:08)
    - Overall engagement score was **9.4**, and ENPS score was **68**, which Sivanandh identified as a very good score reflecting employee happiness
    - Compensation and benefits scored relatively lower at **8.6** compared to other drivers close to **9.9**, highlighting an area for improvement
    - Specific teams like Foot Locker showed low ENPS with detractors, indicating dissatisfaction that requires follow-up and targeted interventions

- **Demographic and team-level analysis** outlined the breakdown of engagement by team, location, and tenure (16:38)
    - Jam Nagar, NAND, and Panaji locations scored high on engagement
    - Newer employees (<1 year) tended to be less engaged compared to tenured employees (>5 years)
    - Top drivers included immediate manager and interpersonal relations, while compensation and recognition lagged, especially in Foot Locker and New Era teams

- **Historical comparison with previous year’s data** showed improvements in data granularity and AI capabilities (23:55)
    - Last year’s engagement score was **7.9**, and ENPS was lower at **16**, contrasted with current scores indicating positive progress
    - The current reports include new features enabling deeper driver-level insights to support better business decisions

## **Data Access and Reporting Tools**

Clarification on how to access detailed team and sub-team reports was provided, alongside discussion of current limitations and user expectations.

- **Report builder tool capabilities and limitations** were demonstrated, showing that detailed data can be accessed via CSV downloads but AI-based PDF reports are only generated post-survey completion (31:59)
    - Nisha requested a clearer hierarchical view where teams appear before sub-teams in the report outputs for easier navigation and analysis (37:03)
    - Sivanandh acknowledged the need for this feature and committed to exploring options to better meet reporting requirements

- **Process for generating sub-team level reports** was explained using the advanced fetch report in the report builder (35:11)
    - The system can generate email reports with driver scores broken down by sub-teams, though overall ratings per sub-team are not currently aggregated in one view
    - Nisha emphasized the need to see sub-team overall ratings distinctly from individual driver scores for clearer insights

- **Sharing and forwarding of reports** was confirmed, with Sivanandh agreeing to resend the AI-based PDF reports via email for wider internal sharing and review (38:26)
    - Nisha plans to discuss these reports with senior leadership and revert with further requirements or clarifications

## **Action Planning and Follow-Up**

The session touched on next steps involving internal discussions and external support for engagement action plans.

- **Pending discussion on survey renewal and action planning** was noted, with Nisha indicating she had not yet spoken with internal members but planned to do so after reviewing reports (38:42)
    - Sivanandh asked Nisha to check with Maria regarding Culture Monkey’s past involvement in designing action plans post-survey, to understand the support scope (38:55)
    - This follow-up will clarify whether Culture Monkey contributed to action planning last year and how they might assist going forward

- **Encouragement to target low participation and low satisfaction teams** was implicit in Sivanandh’s advice to focus on teams like Foot Locker and New Era with low ENPS and engagement scores (21:28)
    - Suggested approach includes dissecting specific questions that scored low for these teams to tailor interventions effectively

## **Survey Participation and Engagement Improvement**

The discussion highlighted the importance of increasing survey completion and engagement through targeted interventions.

- **Non-completion analysis and follow-up** was emphasized, with the insight that **24 out of 43 non-completers came from one team**, suggesting focused outreach can boost response rates (12:34)
    - Sivanandh offered to share lists of participants who did not complete the survey to help HR follow up directly (13:22)
    - Increasing participation is expected to raise overall engagement scores and provide more accurate data for decision-making

- **Engagement drivers and gaps identification** showed that while most drivers scored highly, compensation and benefits along with reward and recognition need improvement (18:44)
    - This aligns with specific teams reporting low satisfaction, highlighting a priority area for HR action and communication

- **Recognition of high-performing managers and teams** was discussed, with some managers like Shah Rafik Abdul Malik scoring the highest engagement ratings (26:49)
    - However, dissatisfaction was noted under certain managers, such as Meenakshi and Samantha, indicating leadership impact on team morale

## **System and Process Enhancements**

The meeting revealed opportunities for improving reporting systems and processes to better support HR’s needs.

- **AI report enhancements compared to last year** provide richer, more actionable insights with driver-level breakdowns and team comparisons (23:55)
    - The new features are designed to help HR dissect data more effectively and prioritize engagement actions

- **Reporting interface usability** needs improvement to allow hierarchical views showing teams before sub-teams (37:03)
    - This adjustment would make it easier for users like Nisha to analyze data without navigating multiple disconnected reports

- **Data download options and real-time access** via the report builder allow HR to generate tailored reports but currently lack full aggregation for sub-team overall scores (31:59)
    - Sivanandh committed to investigating how to meet these report structure needs better in future updates

- **Process for sending participant data and follow-up lists** after survey closes is established and can be integrated routinely to support HR engagement strategies (13:22)

summary.notes:
## **Survey Configuration and Customization**

The survey setup is nearly complete, focusing on finalizing question categories, branding, and multilingual options to fit the organization’s needs.

- **Survey questions finalized with 42 total, excluding removed ones, and making all mandatory** (13:34)  
    - Karthik confirmed the survey includes 42 questions with all set to mandatory.

    - He will update question drivers in the backend to reflect categories like "trusted leaders" and "work environment."  
    - This update aligns the survey with the organization's naming conventions.

- **Survey description page draft to clarify purpose and definitions for participants** (03:38)  
    - Karthik shared example descriptions from other accounts to help Janet draft a suitable survey introduction.  
    - The description will explain the survey’s objective and clarify terms like "managers" and "leadership."  
    - This text ensures participants understand the survey’s intent and improves engagement quality.  
    - Janet will review and finalize the description based on provided samples.

- **Branding customization with logo and background image options under discussion** (05:02)  
    - Janet raised the need to include different brand logos for various business units within the INGA Group.  
    - Karthik confirmed the current survey is for one business unit, so only one logo will show per survey launch.  
    - They agreed to combine the INGA Group logo with the specific business logo into one image for the survey header.  
    - Janet will coordinate with marketing to prepare combined logo images; Karthik offered to assist if needed.

- **Multilingual survey support planned, with phased pilot testing suggested** (07:00)  
    - Janet confirmed the first survey will be English-only for a single business unit.  
    - Karthik recommended piloting two business units simultaneously—one English-only and one multilingual—to validate translations.  
    - The pilot would involve about three users per group to test and approve the multilingual setup before full rollout.  
    - This approach reduces risk and ensures smooth launch across language needs.

The communication strategy will use customizable email templates for personalized outreach, aiming to improve engagement and clarity.

- **Default and personalized email templates are available for survey invitations** (09:07)  
    - Karthik showed a default invitation template explaining the survey partnership with Culture Monkey and anonymity assurances.  
    - He offered Janet a range of sample templates to choose from or customize based on tone and style preferences.  
    - This flexibility helps tailor messaging to different employee groups for better response rates.

- **Platform access enabled for email template review and editing** (10:35)  
    - Janet confirmed she will access the email templates under the platform’s “generals” section.  
    - This direct access allows her to monitor and manage communication content before deployment.  
    - Karthik emphasized ongoing support for any adjustments needed during the survey rollout.

summary.notes:
## **Client Profile and Business Context**

This meeting clarified the client's business size, team structure, and recent performance improvements, setting the stage for solution fit.

- **Small boutique resort with loyal team and steady growth** (04:49)  
    - Operates 15 villas with around **42 employees**, many working 6-10 years.  
    - Recently reopened post-COVID, achieving best guest review scores (Booking.com rating near **9.6-9.7**) and record business numbers.  
    - Leadership emphasized character and loyalty as key team assets, with a small but close-knit staff.  
    - Past crises included earthquake recovery and handling internal issues like corruption and harassment, highlighting the need for better feedback channels.  

- **Challenges with anonymous and truthful employee feedback** (09:21)  
    - Previous cases of sexual harassment and corruption went unreported due to cultural reluctance to share bad news.  
    - Current motivation and culture are perceived as good but lack objective, measurable KPIs.  
    - Management seeks a tool to measure sentiment and allow anonymous reporting to rebuild trust and improve operations.  

- **No current urgency, but strategic future planning underway** (12:11)  
    - Client prefers to implement solutions during stable times to allocate resources properly.  
    - Views this as an opportunity to formalize feedback collection and cultural measurement before future challenges arise.  

## **Product Offering and Features Overview**

The vendor detailed Culture Monkey’s platform capabilities, highlighting how it addresses client needs for employee engagement and anonymous feedback.

- **Four-module platform supports listening, analysis, action, and growth** (14:02)  
    - Listening module offers a rich library of survey templates and full service for survey setup and launch.  
    - Analyze module provides heat maps, sentiment analysis, and breakdown by demographics or departments.  
    - Action module enables closing the feedback loop with system-generated and customizable action plans, including Kanban-style tracking and collaboration.  
    - Sustain and grow module drives continuous improvement and long-term engagement.  

- **Ease of use and support emphasized for client convenience** (15:04)  
    - Dedicated account manager handles survey creation, launching, and analytics monitoring.  
    - Employees can access surveys via multiple channels including QR codes, email, or SMS, supporting multilingual responses.  
    - System captures responses anonymously but allows demographic segmentation such as by department or gender.  

- **Anonymous complaint handling and real-time employee voice** (24:29)  
    - Employees can submit complaints or feedback anonymously anytime outside surveys via QR code links.  
    - Automatic language translation supports communication in local languages like Indonesian, Javanese, and Malay.  
    - Platform facilitates confidential conversations while protecting employee identity.  

## **Analytics and Reporting Capabilities**

The discussion showed the platform’s detailed data visualization and actionable insights, supporting data-driven management decisions.

- **Comprehensive reports with participation and sentiment metrics** (19:28)  
    - Displays overall participation rates aiming for **100% employee engagement** with automatic nudges.  
    - Provides Net Promoter Score (NPS) to measure employee willingness to recommend the workplace, segmented into promoters, passives, and detractors.  
    - Heat maps and demographic breakdowns allow pinpointing issues by department, gender, or location.  

- **Deep dive into drivers of employee sentiment** (22:18)  
    - Platform highlights low-performing drivers (e.g., leadership scoring 3.7 in female workforce) and top issues.  
    - Enables comparison across all questions and categories to identify patterns and prioritize interventions.  
    - Offers exportable offline reports for further analysis or presentation.  

- **Integration of qualitative and quantitative feedback** (21:23)  
    - Correlates free-text comments with numeric ratings to provide richer context for action plans.  
    - System automatically suggests immediate action plans based on survey results, enhancing responsiveness.  

## **Pricing, Implementation, and Decision Factors**

Pricing details and implementation timelines were discussed, revealing the client’s cost sensitivity and decision process.

- **Annual subscription pricing based on employee count** (27:43)  
    - Cost for up to **50 employees is US$3,500 per year**, billed annually, including all features and support.  
    - For a **100-employee hotel, the price rises to US$4,500**, with decreasing per-employee cost at scale.  
    - Implementation and question creation come at no extra charge, differentiating from competitors.  

- **Client views pricing as high relative to current needs** (32:08)  
    - Mehdi compared it to a guest satisfaction tool costing around **$1,100 per year** and found Culture Monkey expensive for a small hotel.  
    - He acknowledged value in analytics and dashboarding but sees better fit for larger, multi-location businesses.  
    - Expressed willingness to consider if pricing or scope is adjusted.  

- **Implementation timeline flexible but client seeks prompt execution** (25:53)  
    - Culture Monkey can launch surveys within **three weeks** and recently offers a free trial product until **April 15**.  
    - Mehdi estimates decision in **two to three weeks** after receiving a formal quote.  
    - Vendor offered to send official quotation and initiate order form upon client’s readiness.  

## **Responsibility and Administration**

The discussion clarified internal roles for managing the platform and survey execution.

- **HR staff typically administer surveys** (27:14)  
    - The client can designate a super admin, who may be from HR or board-level.  
    - Flexibility to assign multiple collaborators and owners for action plans supports shared responsibility.  

- **Client sole decision maker for purchase** (32:02)  
    - No other stakeholders involved in the decision process, simplifying communication and negotiation.  

- **Vendor commitment to customer support** (15:04)  
    - Dedicated account manager will handle heavy lifting of survey design, launch, and reporting.  
    - Client only needs to review analytics and take action, reducing workload.  

## **Client Feedback and Next Steps**

The client expressed honest opinions on the product fit and cost, outlining the path forward.

- **Positive impression of solution but price barrier is significant** (32:08)  
    - Mehdi appreciated the product’s strengths but finds the cost too high for his boutique resort scale.  
    - He suggested that Microsoft Forms with AI tools might suffice for his current needs, showing preference for low-cost alternatives.  

- **Acknowledgment of product’s suitability for larger businesses** (33:17)  
    - Vendor Vishnu agreed Culture Monkey is more suitable for complex, multilocation enterprises.  
    - Expressed understanding of client perspective and willingness to stay in touch.  

- **Client requested official quotation and will respond in two to three weeks** (30:53)  
    - Vishnu will send detailed pricing and contract documents by email.  
    - Mehdi plans to review and decide within the stated timeframe.  
    - Email remains the preferred contact channel; no additional communication apps used due to time zone differences.

summary.overview:

- **Open Communication Channels Encouraged** for questions and feedback, fostering collaboration and ensuring smooth project progression.

summary.notes:
## **Customer Success Team Setup and Partnership Restart**

The meeting re-established the partnership with a strong customer success team to ensure smooth project delivery and ongoing support.

- **Introduction of Dedicated Team Members** centered on customer success and implementation (00:08)  
    - **Gautam K** leads customer experience and will have monthly check-ins with the client.  
    - **Karthik Rao** is the solutions manager responsible for implementation, training, and daily support during the survey.  
    - **Karthik N (KN)** serves as the customer success manager focusing on maximizing product value aligned with client goals.  
    - The team is assembled to provide seamless support and maintain continuous engagement through the project lifecycle.

- **Renewed Commitment to Partnership** emphasizing continuity from previous collaboration (00:08)  
    - Sunil Johnson highlighted this is a continuation, not a new start, reinforcing trust.  
    - Gautam noted extensive internal discussions to ensure the partnership is back on track.  
    - The client expressed confidence in the team setup and readiness to proceed.

## **Employee Data Management and Integration**

Clear plan established for employee data handling with flexibility on format and integration approach.

- **Employee Data Parameters and Hierarchy Clarification** discussed to maximize insights (03:12)  
    - Default employee data includes names, types, and attributes such as manager email for hierarchy mapping.  
    - More parameters beyond managers, departments, and locations improve survey analysis depth.  
    - Unique identifiers (employee ID or email) must be chosen for accurate mapping.  
    - Manager-employee relationships define hierarchy and are crucial for correct data structure.

- **Manual Data Upload Chosen due to Pending SAP Integration** planned for summer or early fall (06:07)  
    - Client will extract Excel files from payroll system as done two years ago.  
    - Format will be similar to previous files, updated with recent organizational changes.  
    - Karthik Rao will provide the required file template to streamline data extraction.  
    - Manual upload will continue until SAP integration is completed, ensuring no delays.

- **Data Update Flexibility before Survey Launch** allows adjusting for staff changes (13:13)  
    - Data can be updated until the survey launch day to include new hires or remove leavers.  
    - Post-survey data corrections are possible after survey closes for accuracy.  
    - This flexibility reduces risk of outdated or inaccurate participation data.  
    - The team aims for a quick turnaround of 1-2 days to upload and validate data.

## **Survey Design and Timeline**

The survey question set and timing align with organizational goals and seasonal constraints.

- **Survey Questions to Blend Old and New** maintaining format consistency (08:04)  
    - Client will share previous 2024 questions plus new ones for 2026 survey.  
    - Culture Monkey team to review and recommend question adjustments if needed.  
    - Final decision on question set remains with the client to fit organizational needs.

- **Survey Launch Targeted for Mid-May with Three-Week Duration** (08:52)  
    - Goal to present results to local leaders in June and organization-wide before July.  
    - July is vacation month in Norway, so timely reporting is critical.  
    - Three-week survey window balances response collection and timely analysis.  
    - This timeline guides data delivery and question finalization deadlines.

## **Reporting and Data Presentation**

Reporting formats will be tailored to client needs with options for automation and customization.

- **Standard Automated Reports Offered Immediately Post-Survey** (10:09)  
    - Includes XLS heat maps and summary reports for leadership overview.  
    - Detailed PDF reports (15-25 pages) cover team and location insights with visual data.  
    - Automated reports provide baseline insights quickly after survey closes.

- **Customizable PowerPoint Reports Requested for Leadership Presentations** (12:18)  
    - Client needs localized reports per location and a national-level report for all employees.  
    - Templates compatible with client’s standard PowerPoint styles will be used.  
    - Culture Monkey will share multiple sample reports for client review and feedback.  
    - Custom reports can be adjusted to include additional breakdowns or branding.

## **Survey Participation Criteria and Anonymity Standards**

Guidance provided on employee eligibility and minimum group sizes to ensure valid results.

- **Participation Thresholds for New Employees Discussed** (14:49)  
    - Recommended to exclude employees with less than 30 days tenure from survey.  
    - Option to include them but filter data offline was also considered.  
    - Sunil Johnson noted typical practice is skipping those under one month tenure.  
    - This filtering helps maintain survey relevance and data quality.

- **Minimum Group Size for Anonymity Set Between 3 to 6 Employees** (15:54)  
    - Default Culture Monkey setting is 3, but client considered 5 or 6 for smaller teams.  
    - Karthik Rao cautioned that too high a threshold limits detailed subgroup analysis.  
    - Sunil Johnson supports client preference for 5, aligning with prior surveys.  
    - Final decision pending client’s internal review of smallest team sizes.

## **Project Coordination and Next Steps**

Clear communication channels and timelines established to support upcoming workload and vacation periods.

- **Three Email Threads to Track Data, Questions, and IT Whitelisting** created for clarity (09:20)  
    - This structure helps avoid backtracking and ensures progress visibility.  
    - IT whitelisting details to be resent due to client’s recent IT updates.  
    - Client appreciates tracking approach for smooth collaboration.

- **Client Vacation from April 3 to April 13 Acknowledged with Work Plan** (17:55)  
    - Team will initiate all necessary threads before vacation starts.  
    - Work can pause or slow during absence, then resume quickly upon return.  
    - Sunil Johnson reassured client of full team support during this period.  
    - This planning prevents delays and sets expectations for task handoffs.

- **Open Communication Encouraged for Questions and Feedback** (18:52)  
    - Karthik and Sunil invited client to reach out anytime for clarifications.  
    - Emphasis on proactive engagement to avoid issues.  
    - Client expressed satisfaction with meeting and readiness to proceed.  
    - The approach fosters trust and collaborative momentum.
